original_test_intent: Remove the approved VLAN from its bond or named parent without error, delete only its authorized persistent definition and leave the parent, management and dependent network state healthy.
original_method: Inventory target ownership/dependencies, back up persistent configuration, bring down and remove the exact VLAN through its network manager, verify runtime and authorized persistent absence, and validate parent plus service health.
manual_activity: User/network owner identifies exact target, dependencies and runtime/persistent scope and approves backup/rollback; operator retains OOB recovery; agent removes once through the supported owner.
required_inputs: Exact bond/parent and VLAN ID/interface name
Verified configuration backup and supported remove/restore procedure
Independent OOB/console, recovery owner and invalid-run policy
safety_requirements: Prove target identity and no unauthorized active dependency before removal
Back up exact persistent definition and use owning manager/API
Stop on wrong target, manager conflict, management loss, parent instability or unexpected topology change
Issue one tracked removal only; no second delete after success
Do not blind-rm, reload unrelated networking, reboot or auto-retry
agent_execution_scope: Bring down and remove exact approved VLAN once through supported owner
Verify runtime/persistent absence and parent/service health
Do not choose target/scope, delete unrelated files/interfaces, auto-recover/retry or issue verdict
engineer_actions: Approve target, dependent-service impact and persistent scope
Review removal/final evidence and issue PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Unsafe and ambiguous: sample values, invalid duplicate deletion and no persistent owner/dependency handling can damage unrelated network state.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Remove the identity-locked VLAN once through NetworkManager/systemd-networkd/iproute2 as authoritative, modifying persistent configuration only after explicit approval and backup.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Bring-down, remove-from-bond/interface, authorized persistent cleanup, no-error criteria and 5/0 timing fields are preserved.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use an ownership-aware single-transaction removal with exact backup and complete topology/service verification.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Replaces blind legacy commands and rm with scoped supported cleanup and rollback evidence.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Runtime down/removal and approved persistence deletion remain mandatory.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Network managers may recreate a runtime VLAN from persistent config or reject external deletion; owner state and boot persistence must be checked together.

project_override_considerations: If the VLAN is not owned by legacy ifcfg scripts, the literal rm step is inapplicable and the owner-supported equivalent must be approved without deleting unrelated state.
expected_evidence: Tracked down/removal and explicitly approved config change with exit status
Post-state showing target absent and unrelated VLANs/routes unchanged
Parent bond, management, services and complete logs healthy
Rollback readiness/recovery notes and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Master's removal intent is clear; legacy mechanisms require a supported equivalent but do not create competing test intent.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Target/owner/backup inputs are execution prerequisites, not a static-review block.

review_improvement: Makes destructive VLAN cleanup exact, owner-aware and recoverable while retaining both runtime and authorized persistent removal coverage.
independent_technical_reasoning: A VLAN can exist simultaneously as a kernel link and manager-owned persistent profile; deleting only one may either be temporary or cause the manager to recreate it. Correct removal must therefore identify both layers, dependencies and the parent bond, then prove unrelated network state remained unchanged.
